# Calum Lill

Calum Lill is a British actor known for his portrayal of the manipulative solicitor Joel Deering on the ITV soap opera *Coronation Street* , . His performance in the role became central to some of the show's most significant and controversial storylines between 2023 and 2025, bringing him national recognition , . Before this breakthrough, Lill had a varied career in television, film, and theatre, demonstrating a sustained effort within the acting profession over many years , . He is also recognized for his work in live performance, notably starring in pantomimes and winning awards for his contributions to London's fringe theatre scene , . His career trajectory, marked by perseverance through a prolonged period of precarity, serves as a case study in the modern acting journey , .

## Early Life and Career Trajectory

Calum Lill's path to professional acting was characterized by a decade-long period of dedicated struggle, financial instability, and the necessity of holding down various non-acting jobs to sustain himself while pursuing his craft , . He is identified as a working-class northern actor from Manchester, a background that informs his perspective and connection to his native region . The duration of his pre-breakthrough career is consistently cited as approximately fifteen years, a testament to his persistence in the face of repeated rejection . During this extensive period, he worked in a range of roles entirely outside of the entertainment industry. These included selling cars, which he described as a job he "hated" , staffing a paella stand at festivals alongside former *Coronation Street* actors Jenny Platt and Rupert Hill, and working at a junkyard golf club . This multi-faceted employment highlights the precarious nature of an actor's life, where financial pressure often necessitates abandoning artistic pursuits entirely . Lill has stated that after fifteen years of unsuccessful auditions, the emotional and financial toll became so great that he seriously considered quitting acting altogether . The financial strain was exacerbated by the need to support not only himself but also his girlfriend, Roberta McClarron, while they saved for a house in Manchester . The economic uncertainty was further compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic, during which he faced the risk of homelessness, a stark reality for many in the creative industries .

Despite these hardships, Lill continued to audition throughout this period, building experience and honing his skills. His first notable television credit came in 2018 with three short films: *I Can See Clearly Now*, *Sleep Warm*, and *Heads or Tails* , . In 2019, he secured single-episode roles in two established BBC medical dramas: he played Chez Wilson-Needham in one episode of *Holby City* and Conor Henson in one episode of *Doctors* , . These early roles provided valuable on-set experience but did not lead to more substantial commitments. His next significant television appearance was a twelve-episode arc as P.C. Carlton Smith in the Channel 4 soap opera *Hollyoaks*, which began in March 2021 , , . This recurring role demonstrated a step up in screen time and visibility, establishing him as a familiar face in daytime television. However, his career trajectory was again disrupted around the 2020 lockdown, which impacted the early stages of his professional development . This history of intermittent success underscores the challenging and often unpredictable nature of a career in acting, where opportunities can be fleeting and dependent on external factors beyond an individual's control. The contrast between this period of struggle and his subsequent success is a defining feature of his biography, illustrating a journey of resilience and dedication to his chosen profession.

## Breakthrough Role in *Coronation Street*

Lill's casting as Joel Deering in *Coronation Street* in 2023 marked a pivotal moment in his career, representing both a culmination of his long efforts and a new chapter of professional fulfillment , . The role was secured after a protracted period of auditioning, and its cultural significance, particularly within Northern England, made landing it an exceptionally meaningful achievement for Lill . He described the experience as "the most incredible thing," highlighting the prestige associated with appearing on the nation's longest-running soap opera . His tenure on the show lasted for approximately one year, concluding in explosive storylines that cemented his character as one of the series' most notorious villains , . Prior to joining the cast, Lill revealed in interviews that he had been without work for a period of two years, making the opportunity all the more crucial , . The intensity of the production schedule was demanding; he worked approximately fifteen-hour days during peak filming, waking at 5:30 am and spending an additional two hours each night learning lines, a grueling routine that he found to be both the hardest and the happiest professional period of his life . This intense preparation and performance phase lasted for about three or four months, during which he struggled for six months to fully embody the character's duplicitous nature , .

The narrative arc for Joel Deering was meticulously crafted by the show's writers, who deliberately concealed his true intentions to create a red herring and build suspense . From the outset, Lill was cast as a "sinister villain," and the character was given a "dodgy backstory" to mask his malevolent core . This strategic ambiguity was a key element of the marketing for his arrival, generating intrigue among viewers. Co-star Channique Sterling-Brown, who played his love interest Dee-Dee Bailey, confirmed in an interview that the plan for Joel to become a murderer was always in place from the moment of his casting in 2023 . This foresight allowed the writers to construct a complex and multi-layered plot that would unfold over many episodes. The storyline involved Joel's initial relationship with Dee-Dee, followed by his darker dealings with teen character Lauren Bolton , . His character's crimes were extensive, including coercion, abuse, and abduction, which culminated in a major reveal in May 2025 . The complexity of the plot was underscored by the fact that even Lill himself was kept in the dark about the full extent of his character's actions until shortly before filming began. He learned approximately two months prior to shooting that Lauren would ultimately be revealed as his killer, a revelation he described as "soap justice" . The final scenes of his character's on-screen life were filmed at the Gorton studios in Manchester, a facility shared with productions like *Peaky Blinders*, utilizing green screen, special effects, and multiple cameras over shoots lasting approximately twelve hours . Despite his character's demise, Lill returned to the set to film flashback scenes posthumously, ensuring the full truth behind Joel's crimes could be revealed to the audience . This planned exit, intended to be finite due to the contractual restrictions on *Coronation Street* actors performing in pantomimes, was consistent with the writers' vision for the character's dramatic conclusion .

## Portrayal of Joel Deering

Joel Deering, portrayed by Calum Lill, is a deeply complex and sinister antagonist whose presence on *Coronation Street* catalyzed some of the show's most harrowing and socially resonant storylines , . Initially introduced as a duty solicitor and fiancé of Dee-Dee Bailey, Joel presented a respectable public persona that masked a manipulative and violent nature , . His character was built upon a foundation of deception, with the writers crafting a "dodgy backstory" to conceal his true intentions and serve as a red herring early in his tenure . This deliberate ambiguity was central to his introduction, allowing him to operate under the radar while committing a series of escalating crimes. His storyline quickly veered into darkness, focusing on his predatory behavior towards teen character Lauren Bolton , . The narrative arc involved Joel grooming, coercing, and physically abusing Lauren, actions that formed the core of his villainy , . The violence reached a climax when Joel attacked Lauren with a chair leg, causing her to go into hiding and prompting an investigation into her disappearance , . To cover his tracks, he manipulated the investigation by framing an innocent man, Nathan Curtis, and coercing him into pleading guilty to a crime he did not commit .

One of the most shocking aspects of Joel's character was his attempt to murder Lauren Bolton's unborn child. He drugged her and caused her to go into premature labour, an act of extreme violence that demonstrated the depths of his depravity . Following this attack, he tried to kill Lauren herself, attempting to strangle her boyfriend Max Turner in the process . The culmination of his reign of terror saw him severely beating Lauren, leading to his apparent suicide attempt and subsequent death on-screen on September 27, 2024 , . However, the narrative did not end with his death. The storyline evolved into Coronation Street’s "biggest ever whodunnit," with Joel's murder being investigated by police officer DC Kit Green . Lill returned to film flashback scenes that revealed Joel's complete pattern of abuse and manipulation, showing how he had blackmailed Ellie Benton into giving false testimony against Nathan Curtis and threatened DS Lisa Swain after she discovered his misconduct , . The plot concluded with Lauren Bolton confessing to killing Joel with a rock, providing a form of "soap justice" for the vicious attacks she had endured , . Throughout this entire arc, Joel was the father of Lauren's newborn son, Frankie, a secret he kept hidden, adding another layer of betrayal to his character , .

To prepare for such a demanding and psychologically taxing role, Calum Lill undertook extensive research to ensure authenticity and sensitivity toward the subject matter . He engaged in meetings with trauma charities to better understand the experiences of survivors of abuse. He also watched documentaries on real-life offenders, such as Ted Bundy, and read psychological papers to inform his performance . This methodical approach to his craft lent credibility to his portrayal and helped him navigate the intense emotional demands of the part. The role brought him unprecedented professional fulfillment, despite the 15-hour workdays and the emotional weight of playing a villain , . Lill maintained strict secrecy about the full scope of Joel's crimes, even from his own family, until the episodes aired . He documented the character's month-by-month arc in a personal book starting in July 2024, a testament to his deep commitment to understanding and portraying Joel's descent into villainy . His performance was praised by co-star Channique Sterling-Brown, who contextualized their interracial relationship storyline as a non-race-centered, authentic romantic arc during the "loved-up, gross honeymoon phase" of their characters' romance . The depth and brutality of Joel's actions prompted substantive commentary from the show's cast and crew, linking the fictional narrative to real-world issues of male violence and predatorial behavior .

## Critical Reception and Public Engagement

Calum Lill's performance as Joel Deering garnered significant attention from both the media and the viewing public, sparking widespread discussion about the character's brutal actions and their real-world implications , . His portrayal was covered extensively by reputable UK entertainment publications, including Radio Times, the Manchester Evening News, and Reach, which featured him in interviews discussing the complexities of his role , , . These outlets provided platforms for Lill to share his insights into the character's development and the rigorous preparation he undertook. For instance, in a May 2025 interview with Radio Times, he detailed his research methods, including meetings with trauma charities and watching documentaries on serial offenders, which highlighted his methodical approach to the role . This level of engagement with the press demonstrates his active participation in the promotional and journalistic ecosystem surrounding his work, helping to frame the narrative for audiences.

A significant milestone in his public engagement was his appearance on the nationally broadcast ITV daytime talk show *Loose Women* on March 27, 2024 . Alongside co-star Channique Sterling-Brown, Lill discussed the online backlash against their characters' interracial relationship, moving beyond a simple recap of the plot to address broader societal reactions, Manchester's diversity, and the importance of authentic representation in soap operas . This appearance positioned him as a thoughtful commentator on cultural issues, showcasing his ability to engage substantively with the press and connect his professional work to wider social conversations. The coverage of his character's storylines extended beyond mere plot summaries. At the RadioTimes.com Soap Awards 2024, actress Vicky Myers, who plays DS Lisa Swain, spoke to Metro.co.uk about the real-world relevance of Joel's character, explicitly linking Lill's performance to themes of male violence against women, female empowerment, and the danger posed by predators who operate "under everybody’s nose" . This commentary elevated the role from a piece of entertainment to a vehicle for social discourse, a perspective reinforced by media outlets covering the event .

The critical consensus surrounding his work was largely positive, with his peers acknowledging his contribution to the show's narrative. Channique Sterling-Brown praised his performance in a March 2025 interview with *The Independent*, identifying him as a "former Hollyoaks actor" and commending his portrayal of Joel . This mention in a nationally recognized newspaper provides independent, secondary-source attribution of his talent and reinforces his standing within the industry. Furthermore, Lill's involvement in the character's downfall was a topic of interest. Speaking at the RadioTimes.com Soap Awards 2024, he expressed hope that his character would receive his comeuppance, stating, "I hope that he does because he deserves to get his comeuppance" . This sentiment aligned with the narrative's conclusion, where Joel's actions led directly to his demise and the confession of Lauren Bolton , . The combination of insightful media interviews, high-profile television appearances, and positive peer acknowledgment solidifies his reputation as a versatile and committed performer capable of tackling complex, antagonistic roles and engaging thoughtfully with the public conversation they generate.

## Diverse Career Portfolio

While his role as Joel Deering in *Coronation Street* represents his most prominent work, Calum Lill's career is defined by a diverse and prolific portfolio that spans television, film, and live performance across multiple formats , , . His theatrical career, in particular, showcases a breadth of talent that extends far beyond the confines of the soap opera genre. He has demonstrated significant success in London's fringe theatre scene, most notably with his performance in the two-hander thriller *The Sociable Plover* at the Old Red Lion Theatre . This production, a revival of Tim Whitnall's play marking its 20th anniversary, was critically framed as "your classic thriller, almost Hitchcockian, with heavy strokes of black comedy and some utterly shocking revelations" . Lill starred as Dave in the revival, opposite Jack Robertson, and their performance was met with critical acclaim . This engagement culminated in tangible industry recognition, as Lill and Robertson won the 'TWO-HANDER' award at the 2025 Standing Ovation Awards for their work in the production . They were also finalists for the same award at the London Pub Theatre Magazine Awards, a testament to the quality of their performance and the impact of the production itself . His participation in this acclaimed, anniversary-marked revival highlights his capability in serious drama and his standing within the professional theatre community.

In addition to his achievements in fringe theatre, Lill has also established a strong presence in the popular tradition of British pantomime. He is confirmed to be playing the role of Fleshcreep, the giant's villainous henchman, in productions of *Jack and the Beanstalk*. His involvement in this festive staple demonstrates his versatility and appeal to a broad audience. Specifically, sources confirm his casting in two separate productions:

| Production | Venue | Location | Performance Dates |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *Jack and the Beanstalk* | Bournemouth Pavilion Theatre | Bournemouth | December 7, 2024 – January 5, 2025, |
| *Jack and the Beanstalk* | Oak Theatre | Scarisbrick Hall, near Ormskirk | December 13–24, 2024 & December 13–24, 2025, |

This pattern of returning to the same role in different venues suggests popularity and demand for his performance. Critically, his casting in the inaugural season of the brand-new Oak Theatre was highlighted as a key draw for the venue, with the press release explicitly branding him a "Coronation Street star" and "best known for playing Coronation Street villain Joel Deering" . This cross-promotion effectively leverages his national television fame to attract audiences to live theatre events. Beyond these major roles, his theatrical credits include appearances in short films and smaller stage productions, indicating a consistent engagement with the live arts. An additional dimension to his professional identity is his role as an entrepreneur; he is a co-founder of Screen Ready, a coaching company aimed at helping other aspiring actors . This venture speaks to his professionalism and his desire to contribute to the industry by sharing his hard-won experience and knowledge. This diverse body of work firmly establishes him not merely as a soap opera star but as a well-rounded and accomplished actor with a significant presence in multiple facets of the entertainment world.

## Biographical Details and Future Endeavors

Calum Lill is a British actor born and raised in Manchester, a city whose cultural landscape is central to his professional identity and the significance of his career breakthrough . As of the latest available information, he is 28 years old . His personal life includes a significant relationship with Roberta McClarron, whom he dated since early 2021 and later became engaged to in June 2024 . This stable personal life appears to have provided a grounding influence during the challenging periods of his early career. His journey from a struggling actor working non-acting jobs to a national television personality and award-nominated stage performer is a compelling narrative of perseverance and professional growth , .

Looking ahead, Lill continues to maintain a busy schedule across different performance mediums. Following his departure from *Coronation Street*, he has remained highly visible in the world of live entertainment. His role as Fleshcreep in the *Jack and the Beanstalk* pantomime at the Oak Theatre in Scarisbrick Hall was scheduled to run from December 13 to December 24, 2025, indicating his commitment to seasonal theatre productions . This ongoing involvement in pantomime, a cornerstone of British cultural tradition, ensures his continued connection with audiences and showcases his comedic and physical acting abilities in a different context from his television roles. His return to the role at the Oak Theatre, following its successful run in Bournemouth, confirms his status as a sought-after performer in this genre , . While specific details on future television or film projects are not available in the provided sources, his established track record suggests a promising and varied career trajectory. His combination of high-profile soap opera work, award-winning theatre, and popular pantomime roles positions him as a versatile and resilient figure in the contemporary British entertainment industry.

The actor has had to keep a big secret about who Joel Deering really is ever since he joined the ITV soap last year
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Coronation Street](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/coronation-street) star Calum Lill has broken his silence after fearing how his family may feel about watching his latest scenes. The actor has had to keep a big secret about who Joel Deering really is ever since he joined the ITV soap last year.

But the truth about how dark and sinister the solicitor is was finally revealed following Lauren Bolton's return. As viewers know, the teen has been missing since February with no trace of her since - until now.

It was revealed in May, three months after Lauren was last seen in Weatherfield, that it was Joel who was behind her disappearance - not Roy Cropper as DS Lisa Swain decided when she charged him with Lauren's presumed murder.

**READ MORE: [Coronation Street's star warns it 'won't be pleasant to watch' as Joel discovers baby news](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/tv/coronation-streets-star-warns-wont-29509911)**

**_Join our WhatsApp Top Stories and Breaking News group by_** [**_clicking this link_**](https://chat.whatsapp.com/CDHYBaprHkXHZsK2i8pk7B)

After making a swift exit from Roy's homecoming, after he was finally released from prison, Joel was met by Hope Stape who handed him a necklace that she found in his car when cleaning it, which viewers recognised belonged to Lauren. Then, a flashback clip revealed him to be Lauren's secret 'boyfriend' and saw him brutally attack her with a chair leg.

For months, fans have been left to ponder whether Lauren had survived the ordeal and it was confirmed she did when she appeared by Roy's bedside in the hospital after he suffered a heart attack following a fresh confrontation with a group of yobs who targeted him over Lauren.

However, as she tried to make an exit from the hospital, she was grabbed by Joel who covered her mouth to cover her screams and dragged her into a family room where the truth about what happened between the pair before the shock attack was uncovered.

In flashback scenes scattered throughout their intense confrontation, it was revealed that Joel first met Lauren at the police station when he was the duty solicitor. He said he'd be her 'knight in shining armour' and it wasn't long before he was supplying her with cash to help pay her bills. But their relationship turned sexual, with Joel expecting to sleep with Lauren in return for his cash and other gifts.

On the day she vanished, Joel lashed out violently at Lauren following a mention of his current fiancee, Dee-Dee Bailey. Joel took off, while Lauren feigned death and has since been in hiding, jumping from hostel to hostel, terrified for her safety. But the biggest twist was that the teen is now pregnant with Joel's baby.

Following the scenes, Calum shared a number of behind-the-scenes images from filming the flashback elements of the gripping episode as he paid tribute to all those who worked on the episode. "Appreciation post for everyone who worked on tonight’s episode of @coronationstreet," he began.

"Every member of the crew was so supportive while we took on this difficult subject matter and worked ridiculously hard for the entire shoot. Thanks to @maggieoliveruk for sharing her knowledge and stories with us to help us create something authentic and truthful. Thank you to directors Kev Boyle and Richard Lynn for trusting us entirely and guiding us through it. Thank you to @ijkershaw for writing an incredible script as you always do.

"@caitfitt0n you are a phenomenal actor. The hours and hours of written work you put in to each and every scene you do is something to behold and I’m so grateful to have worked on this opposite someone as talented and professional as you."

He added: "We had THEE best time filming this!! Stay tuned for what comes next… " And his Corrie co-stars were among the first to respond. Cait Fitton, who plays Lauren, said: "What a talent you are to work with!! Proud of us! Thank you [@coronationstreet](https://www.instagram.com/coronationstreet/) for trusting us with this storyline."

Amy Barlow actress Elle Mulvaney replied: "Smashed it." Lucy Fallon, known for playing Weatherfield's Bethany Platt, shared: "Super duper you guys!!!!!!! what the flip!!!!!" Corrie's Betsy Swain newcomer Sydney Martin wrote: "Absolutely smashed it," while Liam McCheyne {Dylan Wilson) and Emrhys Cooper (Rowan Cunliffe) reacted with clapping emojis.

It comes after Calum told how he was worried about his family's reaction to his latest scenes, which some viewers branded 'disturbing'. The soap star watched the episode when Joel was unmasked as Lauren's assumed killer alongside his nan and went viral after he filmed her brilliant, but disapproving, reaction.

However, he told the Manchester Evening News and other press that he wouldn't be doing the same when Joel's true colours were uncovered in Tuesday night's episode. He said: "I think I'm going to ask her not to watch it because I'm not quite sure I want any of my family to see that..." He then joked: "Or my now fiancée actually, there might be a cancellation."

3](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjc1jOv0Z1sULqEwtlHFnx59jr7NoTnHSfkU9xJz8mJ4IAMWYQ_EQMYGVZo28S59O8M6LVkWH_UxxgxxhZsKN7XmI795CG4tDAlvUHU8EniXLZx-mOl5nO9jJEgqPqvJyEAIGpS0_0t3EYs1zyUHWahVJg5feVJJCbrGOkEYIMB9vyE0591ro-n4eIN5VM/s320/Joel_Deering_Coronation_Street.png)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjc1jOv0Z1sULqEwtlHFnx59jr7NoTnHSfkU9xJz8mJ4IAMWYQ_EQMYGVZo28S59O8M6LVkWH_UxxgxxhZsKN7XmI795CG4tDAlvUHU8EniXLZx-mOl5nO9jJEgqPqvJyEAIGpS0_0t3EYs1zyUHWahVJg5feVJJCbrGOkEYIMB9vyE0591ro-n4eIN5VM/s975/Joel_Deering_Coronation_Street.png) Since the character of solicitor Joel Deering first appeared on Corrie in September 2023, actor Calum Lill has brought something special to the Street. A show with a large cast, it's always a delight when someone with a strong screen presence joins, and it's unfortunate, from that point of view, that his character couldn't be more long-term. But, soap justice dictates that villains of his nature should get their comeuppance, and so once his dreadful crimes became known, it was always going to end with a departure of some sort. As readers will know, Joel's murder led to a 'whodunit' which has spanned the past number of weeks. The culprit was finally revealed in tonight's episode, and so fans who haven't caught up yet should look away now. [![Image 4](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhLg9-u_ntqwKOOEc_ZwEPJgueqXmPZD4DisLNnxBlEOAQ0J1eQx55OTJyJUOmx-IR5L_W5edAs8urtdCZpU2gBFZl-4oTg1LQ6NynYDmRLmFtawqfj8euiOgk4Da8xXr4Yw2JJVJLYhHGNylgyiqgddjeQg_PBO0ILnnpvwMQiyd1VGpHSZT3rvRG9lNA/s320/Calum_Lill_Emma_Hynes_Channique_Sterling_Brown_Coronation_Street.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhLg9-u_ntqwKOOEc_ZwEPJgueqXmPZD4DisLNnxBlEOAQ0J1eQx55OTJyJUOmx-IR5L_W5edAs8urtdCZpU2gBFZl-4oTg1LQ6NynYDmRLmFtawqfj8euiOgk4Da8xXr4Yw2JJVJLYhHGNylgyiqgddjeQg_PBO0ILnnpvwMQiyd1VGpHSZT3rvRG9lNA/s4032/Calum_Lill_Emma_Hynes_Channique_Sterling_Brown_Coronation_Street.jpg) I had the pleasure of travelling to Coronation Street Studios in Manchester for a farewell interview with Calum. He came across as such a lovely person who is funny, humble, passionate, and so dedicated to his craft, and it was clear from Corrie staff there on the day that he is much missed since his departure. We got straight into finding out what it was like to play such a part, and to hear Calum's take on things. Joel's charm saw fellow solicitor Dee-Dee Bailey (Channique Sterling-Brown) fall in love with him, and their engagement follow. But it also disguised the truth of his terrible character, and the horrendous acts he was capable of committing. “At first, because I had to be under the radar, I had to try and be as beige as possible for as long as possible,” Calum explains. But the emergence of Joel's secret wife and child offered some indication that he wasn't all he seemed. “One of the plans was, he can't be perfect, so let's put in some sort of bad background,” Calum tells us, explaining that the intention behind their inclusion was to hopefully throw people off the scent of what were far more sinister elements to his character. His horrific abuse of young, vulnerable girls would be discovered in time, one of whom included his eventual killer, Lauren Bolton (Cait Fitton).
Photo: Danielle Baguley ITV
But this act of murder wasn't a certainty, as it appeared at one point that Joel may have attempted to fake his own death. Asked if he really thought he'd get away with it and escape by doing this, Calum says, “I think he did. He's so blindly arrogant of his own skill and his own ability. He thinks he's more intelligent than Lauren, the police and detectives. In a way, his own sheer arrogance was a big part of his downfall. He completely thought he could treat women how he wanted and it'd have absolutely no repercussions.” The night of 27 September is revealed now to have involved Ronnie and Ed Bailey pursuing Joel with a crowbar, Dee-Dee attacking him, Detective Kit Green threatening him, Lauren delivering the lethal blow and Max pushing him into the river. We're told this final episode was months in the planning. “It was as if we were filming a movie,” says Calum. “One of the scenes we spent about 12 hours shooting, and you've got all these different cameras, and green screen and special effects, and I'd never experienced anything like that before, so it was incredible.” He is so grateful for the opportunities the whole experience has given him, from the role itself to how his scenes were filmed. “I've played him nice, funny, boring, horrific,” he says of the different aspects of Joel's character, “and then I've managed to do the soap stuff, and then on location, and also on this movie set.” The studios in Gorton, Manchester, where his final scenes on the bridge were filmed, have been home to high-end film and television productions such as Peaky Blinders, and Calum gave us some insight into the state-of-the-art technology involved, and the experience of working there.
Photo: Danielle Baguley ITV
“They go out to the real bridge and take 360 degree videos of the whole place,” he explains. Then, in a massive black room at the studio, the footage is shown on a semi-circle of screens, and the set sits in the middle. “We've got this long railway bridge that we've built,” he reveals, “and that's on a table that turns. The camera stays where it is, the train track moves and the whole background is synced as if the camera is moving in the real place.” He says, “it was incredible to have gotten that opportunity. It was amazing. I'm looking forward to seeing it; I can't wait.” Someone who was also undoubtedly looking forward to tuning in tonight is Calum's Grandma who has featured on his [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/calumlill/) watching and reacting to the twists and turns of Joel's story. “I get a text still after every episode,” Calum says. The last one read _Blinking heck, is Kit in the frame now? You really know how to antagonise people. I'm so glad it's not real._ followed by _I watch it every time. You were really bad. That's a compliment. As always, so proud. “_She's so adorable,” says Calum. “I love her so much.” You'll have undoubtedly gotten the sense by now that Calum is such a genuine and endearing person to speak with, and it was lovely to hear what his experience at Coronation Street has meant to him. “I hadn't worked for two years before this,” he says, and while hard to believe given his talent, therein lies the reality of life as an actor for many. He told us, “I really struggled to find my feet as I started, and for about six months, watching myself back, I was just beating myself up. It just took that time to try and get into the character. I worked so hard,” he says. “I just said, if I give this 100% and I leave and don't work for years, at least I know there's no more I could have done.” His typical day during his busiest three or four months involved a 5.30am start, working for 15 hours, getting home at 10.30pm and quickly having food berfore spending another two hours learning lines.
Photo: Danielle Baguley ITV
“I am proud of my work,” Calum says, when asked, “not necessarily 'cos I think I'm great, I've not had the opportunity to work that hard before, and I did.” He adds, “I also feel so honoured and proud of everyone else involved. There are hundreds of people in the making of this storyline and I've just been able to be put as the spearhead of it....I'm the one that gets the credit for it in the street, and I'm so grateful to have been given this opportunity. I miss it here so much, and I miss the people so much 'cos they're just the most incredible people. This is such a magical place to work, and although I only got 15 months here, it's definitely been the best time of my life.” Asked if he's taken anything of Joel's, Calum reveals, “I've got a lot of his costume. His smart-casual stuff is nicer than any of my stuff, so I'm absolutely kitted out now. And I've got the murder weapon at home.” He says of the prop that dealt the fatal blow, “The one that I've got is like a brick that would've been part of the bridge; I've got the foam soft version. Not soft enough to be hit as hard as I was getting hit in the face repeatedly by Cait," he jokes, "but softer than a brick nonetheless. Duncan the director said, _We can tell that you're being too gentle with him,_ and I was like, _Cait we've worked together for so long, make sure and sell this, this is the last bit, go for it._ She did!” Next up, Calum will be playing the part of the giant's villainous henchman in the [Jack and the Beanstalk Panto](https://www.bournemouthpavilion.co.uk/events/jack-the-beanstalk-2024) in Bournemouth. He says, “I was reading the scripts the other day. My approach for Joel was like, _What's he thinking?_ and _What's he doing?_ and listening to dark music with headphones in rocking in a corner. So I was trying to do the same approach for this and I was like, this is a gag to the audience about magic beans versus baked beans; I don't need to tear myself to pieces in a corner listening to scary music.” He adds, “I've got the unbroken streak of playing villains. Maybe one day someone will give me a chance to play someone that's not a baddie, we'll see.” After the performance he has put in on Corrie, I know I would certainly watch him in any role! It was such a pleasure to chat with Calum, both during our interview and afterwards in the Rovers, and I hope more great things lie ahead for him, because he very much deserves it. By Emma Hynes _Read all about my recent trip to Coronation Street in [A Rover Returns](https://coronationstreetupdates.blogspot.com/2024/11/a-rover-returns.html)._ ** Web** [Coronation Street](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/) star [Calum Lill](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46830722/coronation-street-calum-lill-joel-dee-dee-wedding/) has opened up about the struggles he faced when trying to become an actor and revealed why he nearly quit.

Speaking to **Digital Spy** and other media, Lill, who stars as [Dee-Dee's duplicitous boyfriend Joel Deering](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46727525/coronation-street-spoilers-joel-deering-secret/), said he almost quit his acting career before [being cast in Corrie in 2023](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a44944707/coronation-street-hollyoaks-calum-lill-joel-dee-dee/).

"I was selling cars while auditioning for Corrie and I hated it," he said. "I thought: 'It's been 15 years, I'm going to have to drop it, nothing's happening'.

![Image 1: joel deering, toyah battersby, coronation street](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/zvBMjiO5lyW2EPiSVQJVsw--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTY0OTtjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/digital_spy_281/9de38627607bdc8e02c03761cd925885)

ITV

**Related:** [**Coronation Street** **star Calum Lill calls for Joel and Dee-Dee wedding**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46830722/coronation-street-calum-lill-joel-dee-dee-wedding/)

"When I found out I got the part, I walked out onto the forecourt, I was between two cars. My agent said: 'Calum?' There was a silence that lasted for about ten minutes and then I heard 'You got it'. Like the absolute drama queen that I am, I just fell to my knees and was crying and sobbing, I couldn't speak. I was over the moon."

After moving to Manchester with his girlfriend, Lill worked alongside acting to save for a house, describing the experience as "tough".

"Then it came along and I've never felt anything like it. I was walking on air. I felt incredible – especially being a working class northern lad. To know I've got a part in an institution like Coronation Street, it's the most incredible thing."

![Image 2: joel dee dee bailey coronation street](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/nibOEUFf0xcuPSCW7lP.iw--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTc2OTtjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/digital_spy_281/7a40b17d2c58be8ca40af67f165099b7)

ITV

**Related:** [**Ellie Leach addresses** **Coronation Street** **return possibility**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46827391/ellie-leach-coronation-street-return/)

Speaking of his girlfriend Roberta's reaction to him getting the part, Lill said: "It wasn't just happiness for me getting the job, she knew what I was going through and that I was struggling. I wasn't happy in the job that I was doing. She knew that I was putting on a brave face, but how down I was. It was a relief that 14 or 15 years had paid off and I wouldn't have to quit.

"There's no shame in quitting. So many people have to. It's one of the hardest industries to get into. But to know I didn't have to was incredible."

**Coronation Street** **airs on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at 8pm on ITV1 and streams on ITVX.**

**Joe Crutchley**

21:30, 15 Nov 2024

Coronation Street actor Calum Lill has recently opened up about his reaction to the big reveal of who was behind the killing of his character Joel Deering on the acclaimed ITV soap.

‌  

Catapulted into the limelight for his portrayal of lawyer Joel, who debuted in 2023, he initially arrived as one of the good guys. He even began a charming romance with Dee-Dee Bailey, played by Channique Sterling-Brown.

‌  

However, it soon became apparent that there was more darkness to Joel than met the eye. The plot thickened when it emerged that Joel had a history of preying upon and abusing young girls, including Lauren Bolton, portrayed by Cait Fitton. He even came close to ending Lauren's life, leading her to disappear for several months.

‌  

Eventually, Joel's vile crimes were uncovered - culminating in the September discovery of his corpse in a nearby river. Yet, a pathologist later determined Joel was already deceased prior to his aquatic demise, igniting a captivating "whodunnit" saga, reports [Plymouth Live](https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/celebs-tv/coronation-street-joel-stars-three-9701232).

![Image 3: Coronation Street's Joel Deering actor Calum Lill has revealed all on his next 'dark' role ](https://i2-prod.dailyrecord.co.uk/article34093339.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/1_Inside-Soap-Awards-2024-Arrivals.jpg)

View 3 Images

Coronation Street's Calum Lill shared his reaction to the big reveal of who was behind the killing of his character Joel Deering(Image: Mike Marsland/WireImage)

READ MORE: [Corrie and EastEnders actor Timothy West married to huge star dies after 'extraordinary life'](https://www.dailystar.co.uk/tv/breaking-corrie-eastenders-star-timothy-34098336)READ MORE: [Corrie's Carla forced to make big decision as she shares true feelings for Lisa](https://www.dailystar.co.uk/tv/corries-carla-forced-make-big-34106925)Suspects abounded in the following weeks with both Dee-Dee and Carla Connor (Alison King) entering the frame. But the resolution came during the episode aired on Friday, November 15: an impactful flashback revealed Lauren as Joel's executioner following a deadly blow to the head.

‌  

His remains were then disposed of in the river where the police later found him. Speaking exclusively with Reach and other media outlets, Lill commented on his departure from the show, sharing his thoughts on learning that Lauren would be the one serving Joel his long-overdue justice.

![Image 4: Calum Lill](https://i2-prod.dailyrecord.co.uk/article34106155.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/2_Coronation-Street-viewers-speechless-as-Lauren-Bolton-drops-bombshell-news-on-Joel-Deering.jpg)

View 3 Images

Joel was murdered in September(Image: ITV)

When questioned about his foreknowledge regarding the identity of Joel's killer, Calum revealed: "At first, we were all really confused and trying to work out what was going on because we were getting snippets of this and snippets of that."

‌  

![Image 5: Joel Deering's murder suspects in Coronation Street](https://i2-prod.dailyrecord.co.uk/article34106154.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/7_JSR_MEN_031124_CorrieJPG.jpg)

View 3 Images

His killer was revealed in a dramatic episode(Image: ITV)

"And I eventually found out maybe a couple of months before shooting it that it was going to be Lauren. But also that it was going to be so many twists and turns along the way."

Reflecting on his reaction to discovering that Lauren was the perpetrator, Calum wittily remarked that it is "what he \[Joel\] deserves."

Article continues below

He elaborated: "When I found out it was Lauren I thought soap justice is definitely a thing, and I think that's the best justice he could have got."

"He attacked her viscously and nearly killed her, so for it to be able to come full circle, and for him to get his comeuppance from the person he attacked when she was vulnerable and defenceless I think, is what he deserves."

A [Coronation Street](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/tvshowbiz/coronation_street/index.html) star has quit the cobbles just one year after he first starred on the [ITV](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/tvshowbiz/itv/index.html) soap.

The actor, who has already got his next show lined up, will be departing the soap in explosive upcoming scenes.

Calum Lill, who plays villian Joel Deering, will be filming his final scenes in the next few months, according to [The Sun](https://www.thesun.co.uk/tv/29823220/coronation-street-calum-lill-quits-soap-joel-deering/?utm_medium=Social&utm_campaign=sunmaintwitter&utm_source=Twitter#Echobox=1723456414-5).

It follows the latest reports that Bill Fellows, who plays Stu Carpenter, [will be also leaving the programme.](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/tvshowbiz/article-13727447/Coronation-Street-star-quits-bill-fellows-stu-carpenter.html)

In the soap, it was finally revealed that Joel has been grooming and abusing young girls as well as trying to murder Lauren Bolton.

![Image 5: A Coronation Street star has quit the cobbles just one year after he first starred on the ITV soap and will be departing the soap in explosive scenes](https://i.dailymail.co.uk/1s/2024/08/12/11/88437079-13735097-A_Coronation_Street_star_has_quit_the_cobbles_just_one_year_afte-a-92_1723460368132.jpg)

A Coronation Street star has quit the cobbles just one year after he first starred on the ITV soap and will be departing the soap in explosive scenes

Calum Lill, who plays villian Joel Deering, will be filming his final scenes in the next few months

Joel drugged Lauren and attempted to kill her baby but his plan backfired when she went into early labour and the baby survived.

Now, his journey is due to come crashing down as his fiancée Dee-Dee has began to question his lies - leading to his shock exit.

[#### Read More #### Coronation Street's Lisa George looks vastly different from her soap character Beth Tinker as she shows off dramatic weight loss ![Image 7: article image](https://i.dailymail.co.uk/1s/2024/08/11/14/88407861-0-image-a-29_1723381416513.jpg)](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/tvshowbiz/coronation_street/article-13732719/Coronation-Streets-Lisa-George-looks-vastly-different-soap-character-Beth-Tinker-shows-dramatic-weight-loss-emerged-quit-show.html)

A source told the publication: 'Calum has made a huge impact as Joel over the last year but he always knew it wouldn't be for a fixed term.

'He’s been great playing Joel but all good soap villains must get their comeuppance and Joel’s is coming very soon. He’s already landed his first job after the show and so he’ll be finished in time to start rehearsals for that.

'But on-screen Joel has no idea what’s coming for him as his dark secrets start to be exposed.'

Calum has already got his next role in the works as he is set to appear in the Jack and the Beanstalk pantomime later this year in Bournemouth.

Coronation Street signed up Calum, who is best known for playing P.C. Carlton Smith in Hollyoaks in 2021, last year.

During his time on Hollyoaks, Calum had a big part in John Paul McQueen's storyline which saw his boyfriend, PC George Smith, abuse him.

![Image 8: In the soap, it was finally revealed that Joel has been grooming and abusing young girls as well as trying to murder Lauren Bolton](https://i.dailymail.co.uk/1s/2024/08/12/12/88437121-13735097-In_the_soap_it_was_finally_revealed_that_Joel_has_been_grooming_-a-97_1723460589119.jpg)

Calum's character in Hollyoaks, P.C Smith, first appeared in the village in March 2021 and appeared in 12 episodes.

But Hollyoaks isn't the only show that Calum has landed a role in, as in 2018 he appeared in three short films - I Can See Clearly Now, Sleep Warm, and Heads or Tails.

A year later, he starred in Holby City, playing Chez Wilson-Needham, and also appeared in Brummie soap Doctors the same year, playing Conor Henson.

The actor joined the ITV soap last year as new solicitor Joel
-------------------------------------------------------------

[Coronation Street](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/coronation-street) fans have discovered the truth about Joel Deering after months of suspicion. Viewers of the [ITV](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/itv) soap haven't trusted the solicitor ever since he arrived in Weatherfield as a duty solicitor helping Lauren [Bolton](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/bolton).

But his eyes soon wandered elsewhere and was soon inviting Weatherfield solicitor Dee-Dee Bailey out for a drink, explaining that he needed to pick her brain about US law. But it was actually just a ruse as he hoped to land a date with Dee-Dee and the pair have since slipped into a relationship.

However, Dee-Dee was left gutted in recent scenes as, after some digging from Alya Nazir, Joel was left confessing the truth to his new girlfriend - that he has a wife and a one-year-old daughter.

**READ MORE: [Coronation Street star 'burst out crying' over storyline as co-star sweetly thanks him](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/tv/coronation-street-star-burst-out-28687198)**

**READ MORE: [Read more of our Coronation Street stories here](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/coronation-street)**

Joel has now been left begging for Dee-Dee's forgiveness, explaining that he is in the process of divorcing his wife but has been battling to see his young daughter.

But with Joel at the forefront of Corrie's latest scandal, what do we know about the actor who plays him, Calum Lill? Before joining Corrie, Calum could be found flogging cars as he took on different jobs - including a stint at Junkyard Golf Club - in between acting gigs - which included an appearance in 2021 on Hollyoaks in which he played PC Carlton Smith in the Channel 4 soap.

But Calum's big break actually came shortly after he graduated. "I had one episode on Doctors – it was two days filming and you’d think I’d just been cast as the lead in the new Scorsese epic," he laughed when speaking to the Manchester Evening News. He went on: "Then I did an episode on Holby City which was fantastic and then lockdown hit... That threw a spanner in the works."

And Calum was soon creating a link with some former Corrie stars. After eventually getting 12 episodes of Hollyoaks in 2021, he ended up working on a paella stand at festivals, working for Jenny Platt and Rupert Hill.

"The owner of it, his brother is Rupert \[Hill\] and his partner Jenny \[Platt\], they used to be in Coronation Street," he said, speaking of the actors who portrayed Jamie Baldwin and Violet Wilson in the show with it recently confirmed that Jenny will be temporarily returning to the cobbles.

He added: "I’d had an unsuccessful audition at Corrie before and they said, 'If they like you, they will get you back in, do not worry'. I was a bit down because if you’re working class and northern, all you want to do is something on Coronation Street."

Calum has moved to Manchester with his girlfriend and worked alongside acting to save for a house, describing the experience as "tough". He went on: "Then it came along and I've never felt anything like it. I was walking on air. I felt incredible – especially being a working class northern lad. To know I've got a part in an institution like Coronation Street, it's the most incredible thing."

Speaking of his girlfriend Roberta Mcclarron's reaction to him getting the part, Lill said: "It wasn't just happiness for me getting the job, she knew what I was going through and that I was struggling. I wasn't happy in the job that I was doing. She knew that I was putting on a brave face, but how down I was. It was a relief that 14 or 15 years had paid off and I wouldn't have to quit. There's no shame in quitting. So many people have to. It's one of the hardest industries to get into. But to know I didn't have to was incredible."

And Calum and Roberta, who works in PR and marketing, are very clearly loved-up. Back in early December, the pair celebrated their anniversary fo Calum sharing a string of snaps of them both on social media. "Three years of mischief," he typed in the Instagram caption, adding: "Here’s to many more. Love you @robertamcclarron."

Winners of the Inaugural

London Pub Theatre of the Year Awards 2019

The inaugural London Pub Theatre of the Year Awards took place at Lion and Unicorn Theatre in Kentish Town on Sunday 27 October. Eighteen pub theatres were in the running for the major title of LONDON PUB THEATRE OF THE YEAR 2019. Run by London Pub Theatres Magazine the event also includes two awards for personal achievement, and joint runners up to the London Pub Theatre of the Year Award.

The Awards winners are as follows:

LONDON PUB THEATRE OF THE YEAR 2019 is awarded to Adam Spreadbury-Maher (Artistic Director) KING’S HEAD THEATRE

King’s Head team lead by Artistic Director Adam Spreadbury-Maher has an outstanding track record for nurturing theatre talent through associate companies, individual artists and the King’s Head director’s training programme. Spreadbury-Maher has also championed fair pay with an equity agreement in unfunded fringe theatres which has had a positive knock on effect in the industry. He has also made a commitment to opera and LGBTQ queer theatre, which has resulted in opera being more accessible and queer stories being enjoyed by all.

LONDON PUB THEATRE OF THE YEAR 2019 JOINT RUNNERS-UP awarded to

Kate Bannister (Artistic Director) and Karl Swinyard (Executive Producer), JACK STUDIO THEATRE

And

Matthew Parker (Artistic Director), THE HOPE THEATRE

Both theatres can boast high quality work with excellent in-house productions.

Jack Studio theatre has very imaginative productions and has built up a very loyal local audience. The theatre is very welcoming and is accessible as it’s ground floor.  They are also very supportive of new writing and new artists, nurturing some of the most extraordinary talent coming onto the fringe scene.  It also has outstanding technical capabilities.

The Hope Theatre, Islington has an eclectic programme, and is open to new material. Despite being the smallest pub theatre with limitations of space, there’s a lot of invention shown by directors in laying it out in ways that both involve the audience directly and at other times maintain a fourth wall when that’s needed, too.   It does remarkably well to make itself a distinctive venue that competes on quality with much larger venues.

LONDON PUB THEATRES LIFE-TIME ACHIEVEMENT AWARD goes to Léonie Scott-Matthews (Artistic Director) at Pentameters Theatre

Founded by Léonie Scott-Matthews in August 1968, and still going strong after 51 years. Leonie is known for her support of all creatives and the theatre features an eclectic offering of plays from classics to new writing. There’s a regular Sunday night open mic for poetry theatre. It has recently been made a community asset which should safeguard its future. The best asset is Leonie herself and this award recognises the wonderful work she has done over such a long period. Going up the stairs to the comfy theatre you are always offered a warm welcome by Leonie herself on the door.

COMMENDATION FOR SERVICES TO PUB THEATRES goes to Katie Danbury (Artistic Director) at Old Red Lion Theatre

Awarded to Katy Danbury for her ground-breaking work on equality, inclusion and accessibility.  She has encouraged creative and thoughtful ways of integrating access into theatre productions, with a consistently high standard of work.  She also continues to run the London Horror Festival which opened at Old Red Lion Theatre in 2011 and continues to be part of the cultural landscape in London during the Halloween season.

The Ceremony

The Awards ceremony was generously hosted by David Brady, Artistic Director of both Proforça Theatre Company and Lion and Unicorn Theatre. A champagne reception was followed by an introduction by Heather Jeffery, Founder and Editor of London Pub Theatres Magazine. Thereafter several pub theatres were given a Mention before the Awards Ceremony began. Head Judge was actor, playwright, and theatre director, Richard Braine who played “Gussie” Fink-Nottle in Jeeves and Wooster, and can currently be seen in Holby City.

The Joel Deering actor has become Coronation Street’s latest villain, however, in real life he is flying high after recently popping the question to his girlfriend of three years
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Calum Lill has been causing chaos in Coronation Street this past year playing Joel Deering.

From getting Roy Cropper framed for murder to beating Lauren Bolton so badly that she went into hiding.

But in real life, he is flying high after getting engaged to his girlfriend Roberta after admitting that they've "hardly" seen each other during the past year because of his career.

**Read more: [Coronation Street star Jane Hazlegrove’s 30-year romance with EastEnders actress](https://www.rsvplive.ie/news/celebs/coronation-street-star-jane-hazlegroves-33806924)**

**Read more: [Coronation Street star Peter Ash’s romance with nurse, blended family and new role](https://www.rsvplive.ie/news/celebs/coronation-street-star-peter-ashs-33631008)**

### Acting career

Calum isn’t a stranger to the soap world, with the actor previously appearing in several popular shows.

He played a character called Conor Henson in one episode of Holby City back in 2019 and in an episode of Doctors as Chez Wilson-Needham that same year.

He enjoyed a 13 episode arc in [Hollyoaks](https://www.rsvplive.ie/all-about/hollyoaks) in 2021, playing P.C. Smith.

More recently, he joined the cast of [Coronation Street](https://www.rsvplive.ie/all-about/coronation-street) in 2023 to play Joel Deering - the former solicitor fiancé of Dee-Dee Bailey who is the father of Lauren Bolton's son Frankie.

His character has been involved in serious drama since arriving in Weatherfield, which included him beating Lauren so badly that she disappeared and went into hiding, resulting in Roy Cropper being framed for her murder.

His storyline is set to only get more dramatic after people were left to believe that he took his only life, but now no-one is sure about his true whereabouts.

### Leaving the entertainment business

Calum was ready to pack his bags and leave his acting career behind because he didn’t think he would get a job that would pay the bills.

“I took myself off to the key safe cupboard. I had a little cry to myself, and was like, ‘It’s OK, you’ve not got it. So close, but so far’,” the 28-year-old actor told the Manchester Evening News.

“And then my phone started vibrating in my pocket, and it was my agent. I walked on to the forecourt. And he went, ‘You got it’. And, like the absolute drama queen that I am, I just fell to my knees. I was sobbing. I couldn’t speak.

“I was getting to the age where we wanted to save up for a house. And I just thought, ‘98% of actors don’t act full-time. Unfortunately, I think I’m in that 98%’.”

READ MORE: [Coronation Street's Helen Worth's life off screen - real name and her two marriages as she quits soap](https://www.rsvplive.ie/news/celebs/coronation-streets-helen-worths-life-32966741)READ MORE: [Coronation Street star Ruxandra Porojnicu’s life growing up in Romania and soap return](https://www.rsvplive.ie/news/celebs/coronation-street-star-ruxandra-porojnicus-32965365)He shared that he was nearly “homeless” during the [pandemic](https://www.rsvplive.ie/all-about/coronavirus) because the television industry shut down.

“Most actors, despite being professional actors, you still have to have a job to do, between jobs,” he said on the ‘Me, Myself and Hopefully You…?’ podcast in 2021.

“Unless you're in the top one per cent. It's a hustle. That's what a lot of theatre actors struggle with. They love theatre, but it only pays enough to cover your rent while in you're in the job...You've then got to go back to waiting tables.”

### Newly engaged

Callum recently popped the big question to his partner Roberta McClarron. The couple, who began dating around the start of 2021, announced their engagement back in June.

He shared a snap of them hugging, with him pictured in a tight black women’s swimsuit in one picture.

In the caption, he wrote: “About time I made an honest woman of her. Celebrated with drinks in the hot tub but Roberta thought it would be funny to remove my swimming shorts from the suitcase. Thanks @dolly\_rose\_campbell for lending me your spare cossie. I think I rocked it tbf.”

Last month, he also penned a very touching tribute to Roberta, who he credited for supporting him with his career this past year.

He said: “Ah my partner in crime. For the last year I’ve been totally focused on my career which has meant you have come second and I’ve hardly seen you. Some people might have gotten upset or pissed off at this, but you have done nothing but support me in chasing my dream.

“On top of your own job, you’ve looked after our home. You’ve done pretty much all of the cooking & cleaning, all my washing, the pots, the decorating, and you’ve taken it in your stride and never grumbled even on the many days when I was gone before you woke up and got into bed after you were asleep.

“You did this because you knew it’s what I needed and you supported me completely. I’m so grateful to have you in my life and that you agreed to marry me. Thanks for being amazing.”

[Coronation Street](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/) star [Calum Lill](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a61547193/coronation-street-spoilers-calum-lill-joel-discovery/) has sparked rumours that he could soon depart the soap after landing a new role.

The star, who plays [Joel Deering](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a61567816/coronation-street-lauren-role-joel-wedding/) on the [ITV soap](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a61612465/coronation-street-jack-webster-bullied-abi-deepfakes/), made his debut as the [scheming lawyer](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a61559542/coronation-street-channique-sterling-brown-joel-downfall/) last year, but he has landed a new role with a part in Jack & the Beanstalk at the [Bournemouth Pavilion](https://www.bournemouthpavilion.co.uk/news/corries-calum-lill-to-star-in-bournemouth-pavilion-panto).

ITV tends not to allow actors to star in pantomimes while they are contracted to soaps, though **Digital Spy** understands that Lill was always meant to have a finite stint on the show given his role as a villain.

![Image 1: lauren and joel in coronation street](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/lnMOJupM06qfvlkX1Wkiow--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTY2ODtjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/digital_spy_281/0459b108d4631e6596b4ca59eb53896a)

ITV

**Related: [Coronation Street star on Joel's reaction to Lauren's return](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a61537676/coronation-street-spoilers-joel-reaction-lauren-return/)**

While Lill’s role on [Corrie](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a61607015/coronation-street-paddy-bever-martin-platt-return/) may be over soon, the star expressed his excitement at joining the production of Jack & the Beanstalk, saying: “I’m really looking forward to my Christmas Boo’s in Bournemouth, when I bring my dastardly Fleshcreep to the stage. Bring it on!”

“We couldn’t be happier to welcome Corrie bad boy Calum to the Bournemouth Pavilion pantomime family this year,” said Martin Dodd, UK Productions Producer and Managing Director. “We can promise you a giant of a pantomime that will leave you full of beans!”

“Last year nearly 30,000 showgoers came to Bournemouth Pavilion’s pantomime, and we hope everyone will join us once more for an unforgettable festive experience,” added Steve Turner, Director of venues for BH Livesaid.

[_Coronation Street_](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/coronation-street) star Channique Sterling-Brown has opened up about the “bizarre” backlash to her character having an [interracial](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/interracial) relationship.

The actor plays solicitor Dee-Dee Bailey in the long-running [ITV](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/itv) soap, having joined the cobbles last year.

Dee-Dee’s recent storyline has involved a relationship with new character Joel, who is played by former _Hollyoaks_ actor Calum Lill.

But while praising Lill in a new interview, Sterling-Brown shared that some viewers had taken issue with _Coronation Street_ showing a Black woman and white man in a relationship.

“I saw some comments about us being an interracial couple. Almost like, ‘An interracial couple on the Street – God forbid,’” Sterling-Brown told [_Digital Spy_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a45429182/coronation-street-channique-sterling-brown-joel-romance/).

Recommended

*   [![Image 5: Meet Strictly’s Adam Thomas, the Waterloo Road star with fame in the family](https://static.independent.co.uk/2023/08/12/10/newFile.jpg?quality=75&width=230&crop=3%3A2%2Csmart&auto=webp)Meet Strictly’s Adam Thomas, the Waterloo Road star with fame in the family](https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/adam-thomas-strictly-2023-waterloo-road-b2417148.html)
*   [![Image 6: EastEnders viewers praise ‘phenomenal’ Bobby Brazier after violent showdown in latest episode](https://static.independent.co.uk/2023/10/04/08/newFile-1.jpg?quality=75&width=230&crop=3%3A2%2Csmart&auto=webp)EastEnders viewers praise ‘phenomenal’ Bobby Brazier after violent showdown in latest episode](https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/eastenders-freddie-bobby-brazier-theo-stacey-b2423619.html)
*   [![Image 7: Meet Strictly’s Ellie Leach, the Coronation Street and TikTok star who grew up on screen](https://static.independent.co.uk/2023/09/13/11/newFile-9.jpg?quality=75&width=230&crop=3%3A2%2Csmart&auto=webp)Meet Strictly’s Ellie Leach, the Coronation Street and TikTok star who grew up on screen](https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/ellie-leach-strictly-2023-coronation-street-b2417202.html)

“I just thought it’s so bizarre, because the relationship had nothing to do with race. It really is just about two people who have found each other, and are really in that loved-up, gross honeymoon phase.”

The actor said that “as a Black woman in the industry, I think we do put constraints on ourselves on how we’re going to be presented, especially romantically”.

![Image 8: Dee-Dee and Joel on a date in ‘Corrie'](https://static.independent.co.uk/2023/10/04/10/newFile-3.jpg)

Dee-Dee and Joel on a date in ‘Corrie' (ITV)

“So whether we are the sexual interest or just the friend-zoned woman or whatever, I feel like we’re often hypersexualised or under-sexualised as Black female characters,” she said, praising the “authentic relationship” between Dee-Dee and Joel.

“I hate when people are like, ‘You’re playing the race card.’ No one’s making it about race. People just see ‘other’ and they assume that’s what it is. But it’s literally not about that at all.”

Coronation Street villain 'quits' after just one year - with new role already confirmed
=======================================================================================

Calum Lill has quit his role as Joel Deering in Coronation Street with the villain set to make a dramatic exit from Weatherfield as his dark secret is exposed to all
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

14:46, Mon, Aug 12, 2024 Updated: 15:17, Mon, Aug 12, 2024

![Image 3: Calum Lill has portrayed villainous Joel Deering since last year](https://cdn.images.express.co.uk/img/dynamic/20/590x/secondary/5558719.jpg?r=1723472278748)

Calum Lill has portrayed villainous Joel Deering since last year (Image: ITV)

Calum Lill, known for his role as Joel Deering in Coronation Street, is reportedly set to exit the soap. The former Hollyoaks actor joined the ITV show last year as a duty solicitor and love interest for Dee-Dee Bailey (played by Channique Sterling-Brown).

Despite making a good impression on the fan favourite, viewers were immediately suspicious of him. It was later revealed that he was behind Lauren Bolton's disappearance, tormenting the cash-strapped teen and fathering her newborn son.

Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT

The storyline will culminate in Joel's departure from Weatherfield, confirming the actor's decision to leave the long-running show. "Calum has made a huge impact as Joel over the last year but he always knew it would be for a fixed ter,." an insider told The Sun.

"He's been great playing Joel but all good soap villains must get their comeuppance and Joel's is coming very soon."

While his departure may spell heartbreak for Dee-Dee, who is growing suspicious of him, Calum already has plans post-exit.

Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT

**Don't miss:** [Corrie's Samia Longchambon declares love for co-star after personal news](https://www.express.co.uk/celebrity-news/1934995/coronation-street-samia-longchambon-alan-halsall-love)

**Don't miss:** [Corrie's Bernie actress tells co-star 'I love you' as unseen set snaps exposed](https://www.express.co.uk/celebrity-news/1934976/coronation-street-bernie-sam-aston-snap-instagram)

![Image 4: Corrie's Joel Deering](https://cdn.images.express.co.uk/img/dynamic/20/590x/secondary/Corrie-s-Joel-Deering-5558771.jpg?r=1723472278795)

Corrie's Joel Deering has reportedly landed a new role (Image: ITV)

"He's already landed his first job after the show and so he'll be finished in time to start rehearsals for that. But on-screen Joel has no idea what's coming for him as his dark secrets start to be exposed," the source added.

Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT

Calum is set to tread the boards at Bournemouth's Pavilion Theatre, taking on another villainous role.

He will be playing Fleshcreep in the pantomime production of Jack and the Beanstalk from December 7, 2024, to January 5, 2025.

### Corrie star Callum Lill says Joel is only going to get 'worse'

Recent scenes from [Coronation Street](https://www.express.co.uk/latest/coronation-street) have shown Joel plotting against Betsy Swain (Sydney Martin), who has been blackmailing him over his appalling behaviour with young girls.

However, he's treading on dangerous ground as he discovers she is the daughter of DS Lisa Swain, who has been trying to bring him down following Lauren Bolton's disappearance.

A fan theory has emerged suggesting that Joel could be connected to another Weatherfield villain, Mason Radcliffe, who is attempting to reform after tormenting Liam Connor.

The question remains: is Joel Deering's time on the show coming to an end?

**Coronation Street airs Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at 8pm on ITV.**

Christmas has come to the Oak Theatre with the new state-of-the-art venue enjoying a hugely successful opening weekend for its first dazzling family pantomime.

**Coronation Street star Calum Lill** plays the evil Fleshcreep in **Jack and the Beanstalk** whichruns at the theatre **at Scarisbrick Hall near Ormskirk until Wednesday 24 December.**

**Tickets for the lavish panto, presented by Anton Bensons Productions Ltd, are priced from £14.**

Calum, who played the Street’s bad boy Joel Deering, is joined on the Oak Theatre stage by real-life couple **Danny Childs and Suzanne Fulton** as Jack Trott and Princess Jill, **Mary Shanker** as Mary the Fairy and **Michael Lawless** as King Bling.

Meanwhile due to illness, veteran panto dame David Dale has had to withdraw from the run – he has been **replaced by the very talented DG Foster**, who stepped into Dame Trott’s shoes with just a few hours’ notice to entertain audiences on opening weekend.

When Jack Trott swaps the family cow for a bag of beans, his mum isn’t best pleased. But when the beans sprout…and keep growing, they lead to the tallest of adventures in the clouds.

Can Jack outwit the wily Fleshcreep and rescue his sweetheart Princess Jill from the clutches of the giant? Or will he fee-fi-fo fumble his chance to be a hero? There’s only one way to find out.

Audiences can expect two-and-a-half hours of toe-tapping song and dance, colourful costumes, fantastic sets – encompassing the venue’s 4k digital wall, and stunning special effects all wrapped up in a hilarious laugh-a-minute script.

**Calum Lill** is best known for playing Coronation Street villain Joel Deering who met a sticky end at the heart of a dramatic whodunit which kept soap viewers on the edge of their seats. His other screen credits include PC Carlton Smith in Hollyoaks and roles in Doctors and Holby City. His stage credits include The Sociable Plover at London’s Old Red Lion. And he returns to the role of Fleshcreep after playing him last Christmas in Bournemouth.

Meanwhile when he is not causing drama on screen, he loves bringing stories to life on stage and helping other actors through his coaching company Screen Ready.

**Danny Childs is Jack Trott.** ALRA North-trained Danny is an actor and filmmaker. Previous panto appearances include Wishee Washee in Aladdin, Potty Pierre in Beauty and the Beast and Simple Simon in Jack and the Beanstalk, Buttons in Cinderella and Rafi in Rapunzel. Further stage credits include The Wish, That Sketch Show, Farmboy, The Snow Queen, and Ugly Duckling for Tutti Frutti Productions in the UK and on a US tour. Away from the stage he is co-owner of independent filmmakers Squad Four Productions.

**Suzanne Fulton plays Princess Jill and is also the show’s choreographer.** Suzanne is a Mancunian actress, choreographer and producer who trained at the Bristol Old Vic and Manchester School of Acting. Her previous panto appearances include the Fairy in Sleeping Beauty alongside Vicki Michelle, and Aladdin. Other stage credits include Silent Cicada at Liverpool Playhouse, The Wish and The Yellow Dress. Suzanne also has her own company, Parallel Productions, championing women’s voices from the north and whose productions have included Parallel Lives at the Oldham Coliseum. She recently starred in her first full-length feature film, Derelict.

**Mary the Fairy is played by Mary Shanker.** The Manchester-born actor, musician and singer-songwriter trained at the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts (LIPA), and her panto credits include Cinderella last Christmas with Katie Price and Kerry Katona, Beauty and the Beast alongside Les Dennis and Jack and the Beanstalk. Her other stage credits include A Christmas Carol and Simon Says, the latter produced by the All Day Breakfast Theatre Company of which Mary is a founding member.

**Michael Lawless appears as King Bling.** Actor, singer and writer Michael, who trained at The Expressive Arts and Media Academy in Liverpool, returns to Jack and the Beanstalk after appearing in the tall tale in Dublin last Christmas. Further stage credits include The Insufferable Loneliness of Jeremy and Scuttlers, both at Manchester’s Royal Exchange.

**And DG Foster is Dame Trott**. Scottish-born, Newcastle-based character actor, writer and creative DG has previously played Dame Dora Crackpot in Beauty and the Beast, Sarah the Cook in Dick Whittington, the Genie in Aladdin and the Joker in the Mirror in Snow White. He also writes pantomimes. His other stage credits include Horatio in Hamlet and Bardolph in Henry V. DG is also the writer and principal narrator for YouTube channel WatchMojoUK.

The Oak Theatre is a **stunning new state-of-the-art 390-seat venue** situated in the sweeping grounds of the award-winning Scarisbrick Hall School.

It champions bold storytelling and boundary-pushing performances, bringing together visionary creatives and engaged audiences to shape the future of live entertainment.

The theatre has partnered with veteran panto producer **Anton Benson Productions** to present its first professional pantomime on the stage. ABP produces successful Christmas pantomimes for five other venues across the North West in addition to providing Easter pantos for more than 15 venues across the UK each spring**.**

The company has worked with many big-name stars including Les Dennis, John Thomson, Kerry Katona, Mark Labbett, Su Pollard and Basil Brush.

**Oak Theatre general manager Tom Cain said:**_“What a fantastic opening weekend we’ve enjoyed at the Oak Theatre – Jack and the Beanstalk is panto’s tallest tale, and Anton Benson Productions and their hugely talented cast, led by Calum Lill, have created a brilliant, imaginative and captivating production for our inaugural seasonal show. We’re also very grateful for DG Foster stepping in at extremely short notice – he’s an experienced panto performer, and has the audience in stitches._

_“For many children pantomime is their first taste of live theatre, so seeing the enchanted look on our young audiences’ faces, and hearing their cheers and boos, is the best feeling in the world. I’m really looking forward to sharing this fantastic production with even more festive theatregoers of all ages between now and Christmas.”_

**Schools’ performances are taking place during the day from 15 – 19 December**. Contact [enquiries@](https://eyeonsouthport.co.uk/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#66030817130f140f03152609070d120e030712140348050948130d)[oaktheatre.co.uk](http://www.oaktheatre.co.uk/)

**For more information and tickets visit** [**https://oaktheatreandstudios.co.uk/**](https://oaktheatreandstudios.co.uk/)

**Instagram:**      /oaktheatreuk/

**Time:** Various times. See website for full schedule.

**Tickets:** From £14.
